subject: Scope question: tenant connectors, sidecars, and network interfaces across hosting variants
messages:
From: Evan Li <evan.li@acme-payments.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen test artifacts + clarification on what is in-scope

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for taking our call yesterday. Our security team is running a vulnerability triage after the external assessment and we need two things so we can close the ticket on our side:

1) A copy of your most recent external penetration test summary (high-level is fine) and any remediation notes you can share.
2) A short clarification of scope: specifically whether the following items are in-scope under your "Hosted", "Dedicated", and "Private/VPC/on-prem" offerings:
   - tenant-managed connectors (customer code that runs connectors to third-party SaaS)
   - lightweight sidecars/agents that customers may run inside private VPCs to forward logs/metrics
   - dedicated GPU hosts managed by Redwood vs. customer-supplied GPU hosts
   - internal metrics/telemetry endpoints (prometheus/agent endpoints) and whether those are exposed per-tenant

We have one medium finding flagged around an unauthenticated metrics endpoint observed in a staging environment. For our internal risk owners we need to know who is responsible for remediation in each hosting model and whether Redwood can produce evidence of the fix (patch notes, staging->prod deployment timestamps, or a signed statement).

If it helps, I can share the raw finding. Would prefer artifacts by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Evan Li\Security Engineer, Acme Payments

Thanks for the ping — clear question and straightforward answers below. I'm copying the language we can send back to Acme; feel free to edit for tone.

TL;DR (short customer-facing bullets)
- Hosted (Redwood-managed, multi-tenant runtime + control plane): Redwood is responsible for the control plane, runtime, and any networking endpoints we expose. Tenant connectors or sidecars that customers deploy into their own VPCs or customer-managed environments are out-of-scope for our pen test unless Redwood deployed them on the customer's behalf. We will provide the redacted external pen-test summary and remediation notes for the Hosted environment.

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU capacity): Redwood manages the GPU hosts, orchestration, container runtime, and network routing provided as part of the Dedicated product. Customer-managed agents/processes that customers install on their own VMs (even if they interact with Dedicated instances) remain the customer's responsibility. For Dedicated we can provide test artifacts that cover the Redwood-managed surfaces (control plane endpoints, host OS hardening, exposed ports) but not customer-supplied agent configuration.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Responsibility is shared and contractually defined. Typically, the customer owns and is responsible for anything that runs inside their VPC or on-prem hardware (including sidecars, connectors, and local network configurations). Redwood's responsibility in private deployments is limited to the software bundle we deliver and any managed control-plane components explicitly included in the contract. We can advise and help with hardening guidance but do not run customer-side testing by default.

Ownership examples (for Acme's ticket):
- Tenant-managed connectors: OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood in Hosted and Dedicated if they are customer-deployed. If Redwood installed connectors as part of a migration/managed-service engagement, those artifacts are in-scope.
- Sidecars/agents in customer VPCs: OUT OF SCOPE in Hosted and Private; IN-SCOPE only if installed and run by Redwood on customer infrastructure as part of a managed engagement.
- Dedicated GPU hosts: Redwood-managed Dedicated hosts are IN-SCOPE for Redwood's pen-tests and vulnerability scans. Customer-supplied hosts (brought your own GPU) are OUT-OF-SCOPE.
- Metrics/telemetry endpoints: Redwood does not expose unauthenticated per-tenant metrics endpoints in production for Hosted; any exposed metrics endpoint found in staging was due to a staging-only misconfiguration and has been remediated (see evidence below).

Evidence / artifacts we can share (redacted where needed):
- redwood-internal-vuln-summary-2027-03.pdf (redacted external pen test summary) 
- remediation_patch_notes_20270401.zip (detailed notes + staging logs)
- network-boundary-draft-2027-04-06.pdf (diagram and responsibilities matrix)

Remediation status for the specific metrics endpoint: 
- Finding first observed in Acme-supplied repro on 2027-03-25 in staging.
- Patch merged to main: 2027-03-30 (PR #1894).
- Staging verification: 2027-03-31 14:22 UTC (internal verification run 027b).
- Prod rollout scheduled and executed: 2027-04-06 02:10 UTC (release tag release/2027.04.06).
- Current status: closed; we can provide the staging verification artifact and the release tag information, and a sanitized screenshot of the verification run if required.

Notes for legal/ops: if Acme needs a signed attestation we typically handle that via their security intake and an NDA; let me know and I'll route to Legal.

--
Marissa Cole\Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Evan —

Thanks for the patience. Quick summary and next steps below (Marissa's language included).

What we can provide now: 
- Redacted external pen-test summary that covers Redwood-managed surfaces (attached).
- Remediation notes and staging verification artifacts for the metrics endpoint (attached).
- A one-page responsibility matrix that maps Hosted / Dedicated / Private to customer vs Redwood responsibilities.

Short answers to your specific bullets: 
- Tenant-managed connectors: generally out-of-scope unless Redwood installed them as part of a managed engagement.
- Sidecars/agents in customer VPCs: out-of-scope unless Redwood deployed them.
- Dedicated GPU hosts: Redwood-managed Dedicated hosts are in-scope; customer-supplied hosts are out-of-scope.
- Metrics endpoints: the staging-only exposure was fixed and rolled to prod on 2027-04-06; we can provide the release tag and sanitized verification evidence.

Next steps:
1) I'll attach the redacted pen-test summary and remediation notes now (see attachments).
2) If you want a short conference call to walk through the artifacts and sign off, I'm available Thursday 10:00-11:30 PT or Friday 14:00-16:00 PT. Let me know which slot works and we'll loop in Marissa and our infra owner.

If Acme requires an attestation or additional forensic logs, we'll need an MSA addendum or an existing evidence-sharing NDA. Happy to coordinate.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
